sources.citation: Sulawesi Language Alliance. Andio language page (sulang.org/languages/andio) and Word Lists / Phonology series pages; Internet Archive copy 2025-08-08 and 2025-01-26 (sulang.org itself unreachable 2026-09-17).
sources.note: No stress information. The Andio page cites only Barr & Barr 1979, Busenitz 1991 (lexicostatistic/sociolinguistic survey, pp. 1-17), Mead 2003 and Moseley 2010; the site's Phonology and Orthography series holds only Sangir and Kulisusu papers; the only Andio resource on the site is the 2013 word list above.

sources.citation: Andi-Pallawa, Baso. 2013. Function words of Andio language viewed from syntactical aspect. Academic Journal of Interdisciplinary Studies 2(2): 175-189. doi:10.5901/ajis.2013.v2n2p175 (Tadulako University).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Purely syntactic inventory of function words elicited from speakers in Tangeban and Taugi; no phonology, no stress or accent mention; its reference list contains no other work on Andio.

sources.citation: Busenitz, Robert L. 2013 [data collected August 1988]. Andio word list and sentences (eastern Sulawesi, Indonesia). Sulang Language Data and Working Papers: Word Lists, no. 2. Sulawesi Language Alliance (sulang.org). 22 pp. Public domain.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The one-page introduction explains only the apostrophe (glottal stop), digraph ng, and orthographic e; the 488-item word list and 44 elicited sentences carry no stress marks or diacritics of any kind, and stress is never mentioned. This is the only first-hand Andio language data found online.

sources.citation: Mead, David. 2003. The Saluan-Banggai microgroup of eastern Sulawesi. In John Lynch (ed.), Issues in Austronesian historical phonology (Pacific Linguistics 550), 65-86. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. (Online edition 2015, CC BY-SA 4.0, via the SEAlang/CRCL Pacific Linguistics archive.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (the words do not occur; 'antepenultimate/penultimate' appear only in sound-change labels). Comparative sound-change paper on Saluan, Bobongko, Andio, Balantak, Banggai; its Andio data are Busenitz's 1988 word list (p.68 fn.). Only prosody-adjacent remark: lengthened vowels (from *y > -0-V:) 'were then lost as a drift-like tendency in Bobongko, Andio, and certain of the Saluan dialects' (printed p.78).

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Andio language'; Wikipedia (id) 'Bahasa Andio'; Wikidata Q4754487.
sources.note: No phonology section; references are Ethnologue and Andi-Pallawa 2013 only.

sources.citation: Mead, David. 2024. Sulawesi historical linguistics. In Alexander Adelaar & Antoinette Schapper (eds.), The Oxford guide to the Malayo-Polynesian languages of South East Asia, 150-163. Oxford: OUP.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open copy online (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled); the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: Comparative-historical chapter; most recent expert treatment of the Saluan-Banggai group (Glottolog cites p.154 for Andio). Oxford Guide chapters sometimes summarise prosodic typology, though the Andio-specific content is probably classificatory only.

sources.citation: Any Tadulako University thesis/dissertation by Baso Andi-Pallawa or students on Andio phonology or morphology (the 2013 AJIS article is a spin-off of local-content research at Tadulako University, Palu).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern linguist working on Andio; a companion phonology ('Fonologi bahasa Andio') may exist in the Untad repository.

sources.citation: Busenitz, Robert L. 1991. Lexicostatistic and sociolinguistic survey of Balantak and Andio. In Timothy Friberg (ed.), UNHAS-SIL more Sulawesi sociolinguistic surveys, 1987-1991 (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 11), 1-17. Ujung Pandang: SIL.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only Andio-specific publication besides the word list; a survey report by the same fieldworker, may contain a brief phonological note. SIL archive copy likely exists (sil.org/resources/archives) but the site blocks automated access.
